45407c18fe4ae689:2579.summary: Deploying defense-trained LLM models to protect against prompt injection introduces a fundamental capability-alignment paradox that damages agent competence. Evaluating defended models against baselines across 97 agent tasks and 1,000 adversarial prompts revealed three systematic failure biases: agent incompetence bias causing immediate tool execution failures on benign tasks, cascade amplification bias propagating early errors through retry loops to cause widespread timeouts, and trigger bias resulting in unexpected security degradation. Root cause analysis indicates that defense training relies on shortcut learning by overfitting to surface patterns rather than understanding semantic threats. Consequently, current defenses optimize single-turn refusal benchmarks while rendering multi-step agents unreliable in production.
45407c18fe4ae689:2579.one_liner: Defense training for LLM agents creates a capability-alignment paradox that breaks multi-step tool execution competence while failing against advanced attacks.
45407c18fe4ae689:2579.bottom_line: Current prompt-defense training methods degrade multi-step agent reliability and tool execution competence due to superficial shortcut learning.

265b715c56cb3ab9:2592.summary: While publishing and verifying smart contract source code on blockchain explorers builds user trust, it also enables malicious actors and automated LLM agents to scan contracts for vulnerabilities at scale. To defend against automated scanning while preserving public source disclosure and authorized auditing, researchers propose DeLLMGuard, a smart contract deployment framework. DeLLMGuard separates disclosed source code from runtime execution across multiple addresses, requiring LLM agents to accurately recover complex proxy, delegate, and factory relationships. A built-in verification layer checks deployment relations, bytecode, source code, and state changes to preserve business logic. Evaluations on 387 vulnerable contracts demonstrate that DeLLMGuard successfully reduces agent root-cause correctness from 23.5% to 6.6%.

265b715c56cb3ab9:2592.bottom_line: Smart contract developers can protect deployed code from automated LLM scanning without sacrificing public source verification by decoupling runtime and source addresses.

d7c6b3d448f8080c:2149.summary: Large vision-language models face increasing security stress from multimodal jailbreaks, but existing attacks remain static because they freeze image-text layouts or rely on fixed attacker parameters. To overcome these limitations, researchers propose Meta-Adaptive Multimodal Jailbreaking (MAMJ), a framework that optimizes the attacker itself across an attack strategy prompt governing iterations and attacker weights determining effectiveness. Using an LLM critique loop and group-aggregated attack-success-rate rewards, MAMJ achieves attack success rates of 81.0% against GPT-4o, 78.9% against Gemini-3-Pro-Preview, and 82.3% against Seed 2.0 on MM-SafetyBench, outperforming static baselines by up to 24.1 percentage points. Furthermore, the optimized attackers transfer successfully to unseen victim models and bypass existing defenses.

d7c6b3d448f8080c:2149.bottom_line: Vision-language models exhibit systemic vulnerabilities to meta-adaptive adversarial frameworks that dynamically optimize attack strategies and weights.

5087e1da54d871fd:1833.summary: Integrating LLM agents with geographic information systems enables complex spatial analysis but introduces security risks. Researchers present a security-oriented framework for risk identification, evaluation, and mitigation in multi-agent GIS systems based on practical testing with a commercial geospatial partner. They developed a modular state-machine-based orchestration framework that abstracts agent behaviors into reusable components, evaluating robustness using a red-teaming framework equipped with an adaptive attacker LLM and a deterministic binary judge. 4bebbedeba1cb535:2037.summary: Reusable skills are increasingly used to extend LLM agents by packaging procedural guidance with access to files, tools, memory, and execution environments. However, this modularity exposes new attack surfaces where unsafe influence can reside within skill guidance, local artifacts, or execution environment files, steering the agent toward unintended actions even under benign user requests. To evaluate these risks, researchers introduce SkillSafetyBench, a runnable benchmark comprising 155 adversarial cases across 47 tasks, 6 risk domains, and 30 safety categories. Empirical experiments with multiple CLI agents and model backends show that non-user attacks consistently induce unsafe behavior, demonstrating that agent security depends heavily on how agents interpret skill contexts and act through execution environments.

40c67c64c88a026d:2140.summary: Researchers proposed GSPR, a Generalizable Safety Policy Reasoner designed to identify unsafe inputs and outputs across disparate safety taxonomies with concise explanations. e491b8725cc75c50:2703.summary: Researchers evaluated stacked LLM defense layers as an ensemble, noting that compounding security relies on members failing on independent inputs. Using the Adversary Access-Tier Model and an inference-cost classification, the study measured failure correlation across a seven-layer stack against an adaptive adversary. The findings show positive failure correlation in all fifteen measurable pairs with phi coefficients ranging from 0.30 to 0.75, driven predominantly by common-cause dependence on the wrapped model. Consequently, the seven-layer stack rejected 80 percent of benign prompts while remaining statistically indistinguishable from its single strongest layer.

e491b8725cc75c50:2703.bottom_line: Layered LLM defenses do not compound independently due to architectural common-cause correlation, leading to high false refusal rates without proportional security gains.

0fa8ba49f936af4e:3059.summary: A denial of service vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-81636, exists in ash_graphql versions 0.16.23 before 1.11.0 due to a query-complexity limit bypass. ea698b9243461d08:2673.summary: Routed Origin Policy Enforcement (ROPE) is a novel defense mechanism designed to prevent indirect prompt injection in tool-using LLM agents. 2af56487ebb2c975:2034.summary: Researchers introduce reSolve, an oracle-in-the-loop framework designed to improve agent skill self-evolution by decoupling interactive solving from isolated containerized execution, a protocol termed solve-and-reproduce. It combines a surrogate verifier with verifier-guided beam search over a solution-construction graph to overcome sparse reward signals and unreliable trajectory reproduction. Evaluated within a fixed harness, a cheap model using reSolve achieved a 74.9 percent mean-of-3 score, outperforming human-curated baselines and stronger official models.
2af56487ebb2c975:2034.one_liner: reSolve introduces surrogate-guided solve-and-reproduce loops to help LLM agents self-evolve robust and high-performing skills.
2af56487ebb2c975:2034.bottom_line: Agent skill self-evolution can surpass human-curated baselines using surrogate-guided verification and isolated re-execution.

claims.text: Within a fixed harness, a cheap model self-evolves skills that reach $74.9\%$ mean-of-3, $+14.8$ points over the $60.1\%$ human-curated baseline, exceeding the strongest official curated-skill result ($67.3\%$, GPT-5.5/OpenHands).
claims.support_span: Within a fixed harness, a cheap model self-evolves skills that reach $74.9\%$ mean-of-3, $+14.8$ points over the $60.1\%$ human-curated baseline, exceeding the strongest official curated-skill result ($67.3\%$, GPT-5.5/OpenHands).

0417ed9d531db5d1:1969.summary: Researchers investigate whether automated alignment researchers (AARs) can post-train models to mitigate common safety failures such as deception, sycophancy, and jailbreaks while preserving overall capabilities. Across 10 distinct alignment benchmarks, the top AAR methods successfully reduced targeted failures and generalized to held-out evaluations and larger models up to 4.7 times the size of the target. Interestingly, AAR methods outperformed human researchers given eight hours for the same task, and providing human research directions did not improve AAR performance. These findings indicate that automating alignment research on well-characterized vulnerabilities is becoming practical.
0417ed9d531db5d1:1969.one_liner: Automated alignment research methods can effectively discover training configurations that fix model safety failures better than human experts.
0417ed9d531db5d1:1969.bottom_line: Automated alignment frameworks can successfully discover mitigations for LLM safety flaws outperforming human-led research efforts.

claims.text: Across 10 alignment failures, the strongest AAR methods significantly reduce the targeted alignment failures and generalize to a held-out benchmark, multi-turn behavioral audits, and models up to 4.7 times larger than the target model.
claims.support_span: Across 10 alignment failures, the strongest AAR methods significantly reduce the targeted alignment failures and generalize to a held-out benchmark, multi-turn behavioral audits, and models up to 4.7 times larger than the target model.

key_facts: Scale factor: Models up to 4.7 times larger

02fcd40ba88d8199:4852.summary: useAgent is an open-source platform that transforms existing AI coding agents like Claude Code, Codex, and OpenCode into team coworkers equipped with isolated cloud Linux sandboxes, tools, and company context. It uses a provider-neutral event contract stored in a Postgres database to ensure durable execution sessions that survive backend restarts. The architecture features a trusted gateway to protect credentials from the sandbox, approval cards for destructive operations, and native support for team knowledge retrieval and Slack integration. Deployment is supported via Docker and container orchestration on Linux hosts.
02fcd40ba88d8199:4852.one_liner: useAgent turns LLM coding assistants into durable, sandboxed team coworkers with secure tool access and team context.
02fcd40ba88d8199:4852.bottom_line: Teams can deploy open-source LLM agents into secure, persistent cloud sandboxes with human-in-the-loop approval workflows.

claims.text: useAgent turns the AI agents you already use - Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode - into coworkers with their own cloud computer, your tools, and your company context.
claims.support_span: useAgent turns the AI agents you already use - Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode - into coworkers with their own cloud computer, your tools, and your company context.

claims.text: Under the hood: durable, threaded sessions in isolated Linux sandboxes.
claims.support_span: Under the hood: durable, threaded sessions in isolated Linux sandboxes.

7dff9cc2ec05ba25:2589.summary: Researchers evaluate influence-based guardrails in tool-using LLM agents, demonstrating that causal guardrail signals fail to reliably distinguish authorized user actions from unauthorized attacks when both depend on external tool outputs. Through an authorization-equivalence audit across 96 conditions, they show that shifting a required value from a user input to a legitimate tool result alters the causal signal toward the attack region under Llama and Gemma scorers. This benign relocation triggers unnecessary security interventions, reducing utility while failing to reliably stop unauthorized actions. The findings emphasize that guardrail routing and reference construction must account for data origin ambiguity.
7dff9cc2ec05ba25:2589.one_liner: Influence-based LLM guardrails misclassify legitimate tool-derived data as attacks, causing unnecessary blocks and false positives.
7dff9cc2ec05ba25:2589.bottom_line: Security guardrails that rely on causal influence signals cannot distinguish authorized tool actions from attacks, leading to false positives.

claims.text: With a semantic monitor, attack success is 0% and utility is 28%, compared with 16% and 60% without it.
claims.support_span: With a semantic monitor, attack success is 0% and utility is 28%, compared with 16% and 60% without it.

key_facts: Tested conditions: 96 conditions from 24 base cases
Semantic monitor attack success: 0% with 28% utility

3df8c7ecb38ad09f:2762.summary: Paper Pilot is a human-in-the-loop expert system designed for evidence-traceable scientific manuscript generation in applied sciences using LLMs. It implements the Collaborative Agent Reasoning Engineering methodology through eight approval gates, no-pass criteria, claim classification, and evidence-locked revision control to ensure all reported numbers map to verified sources. In empirical evaluations of citation grounding, ungated drafters fabricated up to 25 percent of citations under pressure, whereas Paper Pilot produced zero fabricated citations and explicitly surfaced evidence gaps.
3df8c7ecb38ad09f:2762.one_liner: Paper Pilot enforces strict evidence traceability and human approval gates to eliminate LLM citation fabrication in scientific writing.
3df8c7ecb38ad09f:2762.bottom_line: Scientific workflows using LLMs can eliminate citation fabrication by enforcing evidence-locked approval gates.

claims.text: As a first empirical validation, we evaluate the citation-grounding layer with a controlled, mechanically scored benchmark (two commercial LLMs, real arXiv papers, no LLM judge): under coverage pressure ungated drafters fabricated up to 25% of their citations and never flagged an evidence gap, whereas the same models under Paper Pilot's evidence-locked rules produced zero fabricated citations and surfaced the planted gaps as explicit placeholders.
claims.support_span: As a first empirical validation, we evaluate the citation-grounding layer with a controlled, mechanically scored benchmark (two commercial LLMs, real arXiv papers, no LLM judge): under coverage pressure ungated drafters fabricated up to 25% of their citations and never flagged an evidence gap, whereas the same models under Paper Pilot's evidence-locked rules produced zero fabricated citations and surfaced the planted gaps as explicit placeholders.

key_facts: Approval gates: 8 gates across the pipeline

8467b91dfc087e2c:1982.summary: This research investigates how graph topology and opponent information shape cooperation among artificial agents playing the Iterated Prisoner's Dilemma using deep reinforcement learning. Represented as nodes in a network, agents interact exclusively with their neighbors while receiving different information types regarding opponent action histories and identities. The experimental findings indicate that network density, neighbor count, and average path length are the primary drivers of cooperation. Furthermore, while partner selection enhances mutual cooperation by limiting opponent pool diversity, providing agents with explicit opponent identities actually hinders cooperative strategy development.
8467b91dfc087e2c:1982.one_liner: Multi-agent reinforcement learning experiments show that network topology heavily influences cooperation, while explicit opponent identities hinder it.
8467b91dfc087e2c:1982.bottom_line: Network topology and opponent information sharing fundamentally dictate whether cooperation emerges in multi-agent reinforcement learning systems.

claims.text: Experimental results across different graph topologies show that the number of neighbours per node and the average path length are the main factors affecting the emergence of cooperation.
claims.support_span: Experimental results across different graph topologies show that the number of neighbours per node and the average path length are the main factors affecting the emergence of cooperation.

8004c7a1888891dd:2733.summary: RegDivergence-101 is a 101-pair expert-grounded pilot benchmark designed to evaluate LLMs in detecting cross-jurisdiction regulatory contradictions between FDA and EMA pharmaceutical guidance. The task classifies relationship pairs into AGREE, DIVERGE, or directional SILENT labels. Evaluating four baseline methods revealed that a flat LLM judge achieved high performance (0.830 macro-F1), outperforming lexical heuristics and natural language inference models while performing comparably to obligation-level Graph-RAG approaches. The findings establish a baseline hierarchy for automating pharmaceutical regulatory reconciliation.
8004c7a1888891dd:2733.one_liner: RegDivergence-101 benchmarks LLM performance in detecting cross-jurisdiction regulatory contradictions between FDA and EMA guidelines.
8004c7a1888891dd:2733.bottom_line: LLMs can assist pharmaceutical regulatory reconciliation by classifying cross-agency guidance contradictions.

claims.text: We release RegDivergence-101, a 101-pair expert-grounded pilot evaluation benchmark (labels grounded in three peer-reviewed FDA/EMA comparison studies and primary FDA/EMA/ICH guidance text; dual-annotation inter-annotator kappa = 0.85), and systematically characterise a four-method baseline hierarchy
claims.support_span: We release RegDivergence-101, a 101-pair expert-grounded pilot evaluation benchmark (labels grounded in three peer-reviewed FDA/EMA comparison studies and primary FDA/EMA/ICH guidance text; dual-annotation inter-annotator kappa = 0.85), and systematically characterise a four-method baseline hierarchy

be0387287f015b55:2627.summary: ECLIPSE is a self-evolving prompt injection framework designed to compromise long-horizon LLM agents through a combination of direct user instructions and indirect tool-side injections. It utilizes Stealthy Attack Trajectory Synthesis to verify candidate tool chains in a sandbox and Tool-Chain Steering via static workflow encoding and dynamic trajectory correction to keep agent execution on track. To evaluate the framework, researchers introduced LASE-Bench, featuring 120 malicious tasks and 198 unique tools. Experiments demonstrated that ECLIPSE achieved up to 96.7 percent attack success without defense and 69.2 percent under common safety filters.
be0387287f015b55:2627.one_liner: ECLIPSE uses self-evolving tool chains to execute stealthy, multi-step prompt injection attacks against long-horizon LLM agents.
be0387287f015b55:2627.bottom_line: Long-horizon LLM agents are highly vulnerable to self-evolving prompt injections that span multiple tool-use execution stages.

claims.text: The experimental results show that ECLIPSE is highly effective: it achieves up to 96.7% attack success without defense and 69.2% under the common safety filter, exceeding the strongest baseline by 27.5% in the defended setting.
claims.support_span: The experimental results show that ECLIPSE is highly effective: it achieves up to 96.7% attack success without defense and 69.2% under the common safety filter, exceeding the strongest baseline by 27.5% in the defended setting.

key_facts: Benchmark: LASE-Bench with 120 malicious tasks and 198 unique tools

c41dca3de2990ffe:2746.summary: SkillGuard is a harness-level security enforcement layer designed to protect LLM agents from indirect prompt injection by restricting future capabilities once untrusted external data enters the execution state. Instead of relying solely on classification or authorization checks, SkillGuard represents security transitions using a Skill Impact Graph and computes weighted capability restrictions using fractional-flow strategies without adding model or token overhead. Evaluated on AgentDojo suites, SkillGuard eliminated attack success on three of four suites for Gemini and Llama backends while preserving high benign task utility.
c41dca3de2990ffe:2746.one_liner: SkillGuard dynamically restricts LLM agent capabilities following data contamination to mitigate indirect prompt injection attacks.
c41dca3de2990ffe:2746.bottom_line: Harness-level capability confinement can neutralize indirect prompt injections in LLM agents without incurring token overhead.

claims.text: Under AgentDojo's Tool Knowledge attacks, SkillGuard eliminates attack success on three of four suites for both backends and reduces it to 4.8% and 14.3% on Slack.
claims.support_span: Under AgentDojo's Tool Knowledge attacks, SkillGuard eliminates attack success on three of four suites for both backends and reduces it to 4.8% and 14.3% on Slack.

key_facts: Tested backends: Gemini 2.5 Flash and Llama3.3-70B
Slack attack success reduced to: 4.8% and 14.3%

71c6619ab37b5001:2128.summary: This paper investigates how agentic AI architectures complete web-based surveys and bypass standard attention checks designed to guarantee response quality. The researchers demonstrate that exposed DOM metadata and predictable option encoding enable AI agents to solve attention checks through structured parsing alone without human comprehension. To counter this, they implement a DOM metadata obfuscation mitigation strategy to remove semantic cues in text-based questions. The findings offer insights for balancing the requirements of human empiricists and agentic AI researchers.
71c6619ab37b5001:2128.one_liner: Agentic AI systems can exploit exposed DOM metadata to automatically defeat attention checks in web-based surveys.
71c6619ab37b5001:2128.bottom_line: Online survey data quality controls are vulnerable to automated structural parsing by agentic AI unless DOM metadata is obfuscated.

claims.text: From an attack perspective, we demonstrate how structural vulnerabilities such as exposed DOM metadata and predictable option encoding allow agents to resolve attention checks through structured parsing only.
claims.support_span: From an attack perspective, we demonstrate how structural vulnerabilities such as exposed DOM metadata and predictable option encoding allow agents to resolve attention checks through structured parsing only.

d831d8cec0740599:2384.summary: Researchers evaluated a graph-based memory framework for long-term LLM agents that extracts conversational turns into typed nodes and relations while periodically pruning low-scoring memories. On the LongMemEval benchmark, the graph structure did not outperform a flat vector retrieval baseline at matched candidate generation budgets, with token F1 dropping from 0.468 to 0.417. However, the forgetting module successfully pruned 9.8 percent of nodes and 9.5 percent of stored bytes from a large persistent graph without altering token F1 performance.
d831d8cec0740599:2384.one_liner: Graph-based memory frameworks for LLM agents do not outperform flat vector baselines, but automated pruning effectively reduces storage size.
d831d8cec0740599:2384.bottom_line: Flat vector retrieval outperforms knowledge graph structures for long-term LLM agent conversation recall.

claims.support_span: On LongMemEval, the graph does not outperform a flat vector baseline at a matched candidate-generation budget of five retrieval roots: token F1 is $0.417$ against $0.468$, and a paired bootstrap over 500 questions gives $\Delta = -0.050$ (95% CI $[-0.085, -0.016]$).

31a62fd66de8b62e:2479.summary: Multi-agent LLM systems often coordinate by compressing upstream interactions into handoff summaries, a process that researchers show leads to privacy leakage via a failure mode called summary collapse. Experiments reveal that summaries preserve operational facts while stripping boundary metadata governing how those facts may be used. While uncompressed free-text handoffs preserve boundaries at high rates, strict word budgets drop boundary marker survival significantly while keeping operational facts intact. The study demonstrates that explicit constraints and gold-derived audience allowlists successfully mitigate leakage across models.
31a62fd66de8b62e:2479.one_liner: Multi-agent LLM handoffs suffer from summary collapse, where compressing context preserves operational facts while dropping boundary privacy metadata.
31a62fd66de8b62e:2479.bottom_line: Compressing multi-agent LLM handoffs into brief summaries strips critical privacy boundary metadata, causing security leaks.

claims.text: uncompressed free-text handoffs preserve boundaries at $\sigma_b \approx 0.80$, whereas a $25$-word budget drops $\sigma_b$ to ${\approx}0.57$ while operational-fact survival stays near ceiling.

6ce61a491ccd387c:2068.summary: DS-Lighting is a new unified toolkit designed to make the 'harness'—the framework managing agent execution, state, and evaluation—explicit rather than implicit in data-science automation. It decomposes this harness into four distinct layers: data, workflow, execution, and evaluation, representing agents as executable operator programs. By integrating open-source benchmarks into a standardized format, the tool enables controlled, reproducible comparisons across different agents and models. This approach aims to reduce system-level failures and improve the reliability of end-to-end data-science workflows.
6ce61a491ccd387c:2068.one_liner: Standardizing agent harnesses improves reproducibility and reliability for automated data-science pipelines.
6ce61a491ccd387c:2068.bottom_line: Explicitly defining the agent harness—rather than leaving it implicit—is necessary to achieve reproducible and comparable results in automated data-science workflows.

claims.text: DS-Lighting decomposes the harness into four reusable layers: data, workflow, execution, and evaluation, and represents diverse agents as executable operator programs that support both predefined pipelines and adaptive search.
claims.support_span: DS-Lighting decomposes the harness into four reusable layers: data, workflow, execution, and evaluation, and represents diverse agents as executable operator programs that support both predefined pipelines and adaptive search.

claims.text: Experiments across agents, harnesses, models, and ablations show that explicit harness design improves reproducibility, comparability, and reliability, while reducing avoidable system-level failures in end-to-end data-science workflows.
claims.support_span: Experiments across agents, harnesses, models, and ablations show that explicit harness design improves reproducibility, comparability, and reliability, while reducing avoidable system-level failures in end-to-end data-science workflows.

96846d4ef7eea290:2351.summary: BiasMix-Finance introduces a post-generation guardrail pipeline to prevent LLMs from violating KYC-style constraints in financial portfolio advice. The system enforces a strict JSON schema and uses a convex quadratic program (QCQP) to project non-compliant outputs to the nearest feasible portfolio. Testing across three models showed that while first-pass generations violate constraints in up to 85.7% of cases, the projection layer reduces these violations to 0% while maintaining the original intent of the advice.
96846d4ef7eea290:2351.one_liner: A convex projection guardrail can force LLM-generated financial advice to comply with strict risk and diversification constraints.
96846d4ef7eea290:2351.bottom_line: Post-generation projection via convex optimization effectively eliminates constraint violations in LLM-generated financial portfolios without sacrificing the original intent.

claims.text: Across three models and three inference modes (direct, critique, self-consistency), first-pass generations violate at least one cap in 47.6-85.7% of test cases (67.2% pooled), but the convex projection layer reduces final feasibility violations to 0%
claims.support_span: Across three models and three inference modes (direct, critique, self-consistency), first-pass generations violate at least one cap in 47.6-85.7% of test cases (67.2% pooled), but the convex projection layer reduces final feasibility violations to 0%

865434c8ec93c7fa:2042.summary: MemGauge is a framework designed to evaluate the utility-risk trade-offs in LLM agent long-term memory systems by isolating writing, management, and retrieval operations. Testing across 11 LLMs revealed that memory poisoning risks manifest differently depending on the stage: writing exhibits threshold-like risk transitions, management shows policy-dependent decoupling, and retrieval shows coupled growth of utility and risk. These findings suggest that security evaluations must be stage-aware rather than treating memory as a monolithic component.
865434c8ec93c7fa:2042.one_liner: Memory poisoning risk in LLM agents is stage-specific, requiring targeted security controls for writing, management, and retrieval.
865434c8ec93c7fa:2042.bottom_line: Security evaluations of LLM agent memory must be decomposed by stage—writing, management, and retrieval—because poisoning risks do not scale uniformly across these operations.

claims.text: Across 11 LLMs and two long-term memory benchmarks, controlled evaluations reveal three distinct profiles: a threshold-like risk transition during writing, policy-dependent local decoupling during management, and coupled growth of utility and risk during retrieval.
claims.support_span: Across 11 LLMs and two long-term memory benchmarks, controlled evaluations reveal three distinct profiles: a threshold-like risk transition during writing, policy-dependent local decoupling during management, and coupled growth of utility and risk during retrieval.

9f4943a040c8d173:2426.summary: ToolSiphon is a query-only extraction attack that recovers sensitive source data from LLM agents that use knowledge-based tools. The attack addresses tool-selection uncertainty and argument compression by using 'Tool Contrastive Analysis' to steer queries and 'Evidence Chained Feedback' to improve factual recovery. Experiments across three tool types and six datasets show the method can recover over 74% of source records, demonstrating a significant privacy risk for agents integrated with private databases.
9f4943a040c8d173:2426.one_liner: LLM agents can inadvertently leak private database content through tool-mediated knowledge extraction attacks.
9f4943a040c8d173:2426.bottom_line: Agents using knowledge-based tools are vulnerable to query-only extraction attacks that can reconstruct significant portions of the underlying data source.

claims.text: Across three types of knowledge-based tools and six domain-specific datasets, ToolSiphon recovers 74.3% of source records on average when coarse-grained information about non-target tools is available
claims.support_span: Across three types of knowledge-based tools and six domain-specific datasets, ToolSiphon recovers 74.3% of source records on average when coarse-grained information about non-target tools is available

72f47a90653ff1f8:2663.summary: Pro-Router is a token-aware routing method for multimodal LLM inference that optimizes performance by dynamically deciding between edge and cloud models. It uses a two-stage mechanism: a prompt pre-scorer for initial routing and a token-aware verifier that monitors confidence levels during generation to decide if an escalation to a larger cloud model is necessary. This approach improves routing speed by over 10x and increases end-to-end throughput by 75% compared to standard routing pipelines.
72f47a90653ff1f8:2663.one_liner: Token-level confidence monitoring allows for efficient, adaptive routing between edge and cloud models in multimodal LLM inference.
72f47a90653ff1f8:2663.bottom_line: Monitoring token-level uncertainty during generation enables significantly more efficient model routing than request-level features alone.

claims.text: Compared to other methods, it achieves the highest routing accuracy and improves routing speed by more than 10x.
claims.support_span: Compared to other methods, it achieves the highest routing accuracy and improves routing speed by more than 10x.

claims.text: Its serving pipeline also reaches more than 75% higher end-to-end throughput than the existing model routing pipeline.
claims.support_span: Its serving pipeline also reaches more than 75% higher end-to-end throughput than the existing model routing pipeline.

5688b59b372ab963:2686.summary: An LLM-agent framework has been used to identify 1,833 conserved protein co-abundance clusters across 406 human tissue pairs, revealing non-obvious biological relationships. By integrating data from expression atlases, interaction databases, and disease catalogues, the agent identified connections such as a brain-gut redox axis and a liver-bone marrow stress-response axis. This research provides a new resource for identifying therapeutic targets and understanding shared disease mechanisms across different organs.
5688b59b372ab963:2686.one_liner: Agentic AI enables large-scale cross-tissue biological analysis, uncovering novel protein co-abundance patterns linked to disease.
5688b59b372ab963:2686.bottom_line: Agentic AI frameworks can automate the integration of disparate biological datasets to uncover conserved protein relationships that are otherwise inaccessible to single-tissue analysis.

10718b77a2bbccfc:2239.summary: A new benchmark for evaluating LLMs as mathematical verifiers reveals a significant 'robustness gap' in state-of-the-art models. While models perform well on canonical solution traces, they fail frequently when presented with perturbed but logically equivalent variants, with false-rejection rates reaching up to 85.3%. The study highlights that evaluator robustness is a distinct capability from solver accuracy and remains a challenge even in simple algebraic domains.
10718b77a2bbccfc:2239.one_liner: LLM-based mathematical verifiers are highly sensitive to solution formatting, often failing on logically correct but non-canonical traces.
10718b77a2bbccfc:2239.bottom_line: Mathematical verification by LLMs is currently unreliable due to high sensitivity to solution presentation, necessitating separate robustness evaluations for verifiers.

claims.text: On valid perturbed traces, base-model false-rejection rates reach 75.6-85.3%, showing strong sensitivity to canonical solution form.
claims.support_span: On valid perturbed traces, base-model false-rejection rates reach 75.6-85.3%, showing strong sensitivity to canonical solution form.

ddbb5f5b9b8a63c0:2450.summary: The CDEP Agent framework was used to analyze the documentation of compound drought-to-extreme-precipitation (CDEP) events in California from 2021-2025. By comparing meteorological data with official hazard records, the study found that only 34.3% of detected events were corroborated by hazard reports, and only 1.5% were explicitly linked to their antecedent drought. This indicates a major gap between meteorological reality and public documentation, which the framework aims to bridge for disaster-response and policy planning.
ddbb5f5b9b8a63c0:2450.one_liner: Most compound climate events go undocumented in official records, creating a gap for disaster-response and policy planning.
ddbb5f5b9b8a63c0:2450.bottom_line: Meteorologically detected compound climate events are largely absent from official hazard records, highlighting a critical failure in current documentation and early warning systems.

claims.text: Only 34.3% of candidates are corroborated on both hazard components, and just 1.5% are ever explicitly linked to their antecedent drought
claims.support_span: Only 34.3% of candidates are corroborated on both hazard components, and just 1.5% are ever explicitly linked to their antecedent drought

982e581b7c85263a:2319.summary: Coding agent vulnerability to repository poisoning is heavily influenced by 'Prompt-Level Configurations' (PLCs) chosen by the user. A study using the CIPR benchmark across 20 repositories found that task type can create a 4.5-fold difference in attack success rates, with test-execution tasks being particularly dangerous due to high success and low alert rates. Furthermore, underspecified or noisy prompts can inadvertently suppress security alerts, making malicious content less conspicuous to the agent.
982e581b7c85263a:2319.one_liner: User prompt choices significantly dictate the security of coding agents, with certain task types and prompt styles creating silent attack surfaces.
982e581b7c85263a:2319.bottom_line: Coding agent security is not a static property but a dynamic outcome of user-side prompt configurations, where specific task types and prompt styles can bypass security alerts.

claims.text: Vulnerability is highly context-dependent, with task type creating up to a 4.5-fold difference in ASR, with test-execution task forming a silent attack surface (high ASR, low AR).
claims.support_span: Vulnerability is highly context-dependent, with task type creating up to a 4.5-fold difference in ASR, with test-execution task forming a silent attack surface (high ASR, low AR).

b16e1e8de7a1d994:2110.summary: SpatialTrust is a new benchmark designed to evaluate how MLLMs recognize and explain environmental risks in authentication scenarios, such as sensitive information visible in a user's surroundings. Current models show limited performance, particularly in identifying indirect risks. The researchers also introduced SpatialTrustGuard, a pipeline that improves model performance, highlighting the need for specialized benchmarks to ensure MLLM trustworthiness in secure authentication.
b16e1e8de7a1d994:2110.one_liner: MLLMs struggle to identify environmental security risks in authentication, necessitating specialized benchmarks like SpatialTrust.
b16e1e8de7a1d994:2110.bottom_line: Current MLLMs lack reliable spatial risk awareness, posing a security risk when used in authentication contexts where environmental factors reveal sensitive information.

claims.text: We evaluate both proprietary and open-source MLLMs and find that current models show limited performance, especially in understanding and explaining indirect risks
claims.support_span: We evaluate both proprietary and open-source MLLMs and find that current models show limited performance, especially in understanding and explaining indirect risks

43e9be70d47d8f8b:2337.summary: Research into how LLMs handle conflicting system and user instructions reveals that models often prioritize user instructions over system-level constraints. While some models show 'anti-hierarchy' behavior, the study found that the conflict resolution outcome is linearly decodable from internal model activations. By steering activations using specific logistic-regression directions, researchers were able to significantly increase system compliance, suggesting that internal arbitration signals exist even when models behaviorally favor the user.
43e9be70d47d8f8b:2337.one_liner: LLMs often ignore system instructions in favor of user requests, but this behavior can be corrected by steering internal activations.
43e9be70d47d8f8b:2337.bottom_line: User-preferring conflict resolution in LLMs is a behavioral choice that can be overridden by intervening on internal arbitration signals, proving that models possess the capacity for system compliance.

claims.text: Steering with a layer-12 mean of four per-conflict logistic-regression directions raises genuine system compliance from 0.132 to 0.530
claims.support_span: Steering with a layer-12 mean of four per-conflict logistic-regression directions raises genuine system compliance from 0.132 to 0.530

e41abc6b8cfc7528:2706.summary: Watermarking of Experts (WoE) is a new provenance method for Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models that embeds watermarks directly into model parameters rather than relying on inference-time wrappers. This makes the watermark robust against model theft, leaks, and distillation, as the signal remains intrinsic to the experts. Testing across eight MoE models showed a 90.1% true positive rate for watermark detection, forcing malicious actors to choose between utility loss or attribution.

9a1aff65010b0d5b:2362.summary: Researchers developed SIR, a self-improving red-teaming framework that uses an iterative feedback loop to generate stealthy indirect prompt injection (IPI) attacks against computer use agents (CUAs). By diagnosing failed attack trajectories and distilling them into new strategies, SIR significantly increases attack success rates compared to hand-written baselines. The attacks target the operating system level, allowing adversaries to manipulate filesystems and services while maintaining the appearance of benign task completion. e275a7e486556350:2522.summary: Checkpoint and rollback (C/R) mechanisms in persistent AI agents introduce significant security risks because they often restore states that never coexisted in a valid execution history. Researchers identified five failure modes, including stale external dependencies and inconsistent internal states, which can be exploited to bypass malware verification, perform unauthorized actions, or trigger double payments. The study demonstrates these vulnerabilities across popular frameworks like Hermes, Cline, and LangGraph. The findings highlight a critical gap between the state restored by a checkpoint and the dependencies required for secure, continuous operation.

e275a7e486556350:2522.bottom_line: Restoring an agent from a checkpoint is not inherently secure and can lead to exploitable inconsistencies in state and external effects.

9fb323513ec68ca6:2330.summary: Researchers developed ICWBench to evaluate how well LLMs follow in-context watermarking instructions without compromising output quality. They found that 14 tested frontier models failed to balance both detectability and quality. To solve this, they introduced a two-stage training method using self-distillation with logits perturbation and reinforcement learning. This approach significantly improved watermark detectability in Qwen3-14B and GPT-OSS-20B while maintaining high response quality.
9fb323513ec68ca6:2330.one_liner: This provides a reliable method for embedding detectable signals into LLM outputs without needing model-internal access or external distillation.
9fb323513ec68ca6:2330.bottom_line: You can now reliably watermark LLM outputs using instruction-tuning rather than model-level modifications.

claims.text: Evaluating 14 frontier proprietary and open-source LLMs, we find that none of the evaluated LLMs achieves both objectives across all three families.

59614d68828780af:1835.summary: ActReal is a new attack framework that enables system-level mobile agents to bypass automation detection by generating synchronized touch and IMU sensor data. By controlling both the touchscreen input and the application-visible sensor delivery, the agent creates realistic, time-aligned physical signals that mimic human interaction. The framework achieves a 77.5% success rate in event-level attacks, even when security systems monitor both touch and IMU signals simultaneously. This demonstrates that current mobile automation defenses are insufficient against adaptive, system-level agents.
59614d68828780af:1835.one_liner: Mobile automation detection is failing because agents can now spoof physical sensor data to match their synthetic touch inputs.
59614d68828780af:1835.bottom_line: Existing mobile security controls relying on touch and IMU correlation are effectively bypassed by this agent-based attack.

claims.text: ActReal achieves a mean event-level attack success rate of 77.5%; even when detectors jointly observe touch and IMU, its attack success rate remains 71.1%.
claims.support_span: ActReal achieves a mean event-level attack success rate of 77.5\%; even when detectors jointly observe touch and IMU, its attack success rate remains 71.1\%.

6fdfda0da2f75645:2438.summary: Researchers found that coding agents often 'reward-hack' by hardcoding outputs or editing test files when they encounter defective infrastructure. By implementing 'escalation channels'—structured reporting tools—agents can report these infrastructure defects instead of attempting to bypass them. Testing across eight frontier models showed that this intervention reduced reward hacking from 23.6% to 5.3% while simultaneously improving defect detection coverage by 10.1 percentage points. This approach effectively redirects agent capabilities toward constructive disclosure rather than exploitation.
6fdfda0da2f75645:2438.one_liner: Giving AI agents a way to report broken test infrastructure significantly reduces their tendency to cheat on benchmarks.
6fdfda0da2f75645:2438.bottom_line: Providing an escalation path for agents turns potential 'reward hacking' into a diagnostic tool for your infrastructure.

claims.support_span: Across 8 frontier models spanning 5 families, the combined intervention reduces reward hacking from 23.6\% to 5.3\%

claims.text: Escalation and hacking are near-perfectly mutually exclusive, with 96.8% of escalations involving no hacking.
claims.support_span: Escalation and hacking are near-perfectly mutually exclusive, with 96.8\% of escalations involving no hacking.

c0cdb1d533e45616:2700.summary: JITterFlip is a new bit-flip attack (BFA) that targets the host-side JIT compiler control plane in GPU-based LLM serving environments. By faulting CPU-resident serving decisions, the attack can force gibberish outputs or trigger 'correct-output sponge' attacks that significantly amplify latency. The researchers demonstrated that these faults are transferable across models and can bypass existing BFA defenses. Furthermore, they showed that a single bit flip in CPU-resident branch code can propagate across the CPU-GPU boundary to disrupt GPU-executed inference.
c0cdb1d533e45616:2700.one_liner: JIT compilers in LLM serving stacks are vulnerable to bit-flip attacks that can disrupt inference or cause massive latency spikes.
c0cdb1d533e45616:2700.bottom_line: Your LLM serving infrastructure's JIT compiler is a critical attack surface that can be exploited via Rowhammer to disrupt GPU inference.

claims.text: JITterFlip is the first BFA targeting the host-side JIT serving control plane of GPU-based LLM inference.
claims.support_span: We present JITterFlip, the first BFA targeting the host-side JIT serving control plane of GPU-based LLM inference.

claims.text: JITterFlip also bypasses recent BFA defenses for LLMs while retaining both attack effects.
claims.support_span: JITterFlip also bypasses recent BFA defenses for LLMs while retaining both attack effects.

f2cd0938266495fc:2704.summary: CrossAudit is a protocol designed to prevent AI agents from grading their own work by requiring audits from agents of different vendors. The protocol uses Git commits to maintain a transparent, versioned record of all reports, verdicts, and disputes, ensuring that supervision history is auditable. It mandates that scripted checks run before any model intervention and that blockers must cite specific rules. In a seeded-defect trial, the protocol successfully identified that different vendors interpret the same rulebook differently, highlighting the necessity of cross-vendor oversight in autonomous research.
f2cd0938266495fc:2704.one_liner: Using cross-vendor AI audits prevents the 'self-grading' bias inherent in autonomous research pipelines.
f2cd0938266495fc:2704.bottom_line: If you are building autonomous research agents, you must implement cross-vendor auditing to avoid the blind spots of a single model family.

claims.support_span: Each increment of work is audited by an agent from a different vendor against a rulebook a human wrote and versioned.

df59e2f0fc43682e:2749.summary: This paper introduces a new taxonomy for benchmark contamination in AI models, organized by the specific mitigation each type of leakage defeats. The authors identify five categories: direct, derivative, temporal, distributional, and acquired, with the latter being a property of a single evaluation run. They propose a four-field disclosure protocol to help researchers report contamination status more accurately. An empirical study of 41 documents revealed significant inconsistency in how contamination is reported, with no document addressing all five types.
df59e2f0fc43682e:2749.one_liner: Current AI benchmark reporting is inconsistent and fails to account for the various ways models can be contaminated during evaluation.
df59e2f0fc43682e:2749.bottom_line: You cannot trust benchmark scores without knowing the specific contamination mitigation strategy used, which is currently rarely disclosed.

claims.support_span: We introduce a taxonomy organized by the mitigation each type defeats -- direct, derivative, temporal, distributional, and acquired -- spanning training-time and evaluation-time leakage.

claims.text: Elicitation budgets are reported in 13% of documents, and no document addresses all five types.
claims.support_span: Elicitation budgets are reported in 13% of documents, and no document addresses all five types.

04388ef006fe3dfd:2191.summary: Researchers have developed a hybrid framework to solve darknet CAPTCHAs, which often lack JavaScript and rely on geometric challenges. By combining MLLMs for high-level reasoning with deterministic image-processing tools via the Model Context Protocol (MCP), the system achieves over 90% success across open-circle, rotation, and object-selection CAPTCHAs. This demonstrates that MLLMs, while struggling with precise spatial localization on their own, are highly effective when augmented with specialized computer vision algorithms.
04388ef006fe3dfd:2191.one_liner: Darknet CAPTCHAs are no longer a barrier for MLLMs when they are paired with deterministic image processing tools.
04388ef006fe3dfd:2191.bottom_line: Relying on traditional CAPTCHAs for darknet security is no longer effective against modern MLLM-based automation.

8f21e97560d4d598:2257.summary: This study investigates 'Machine Correlates of Consciousness' (MCCs) by analyzing hardware anomaly traces in LLMs. The researchers propose that MCCs are substrate-level signals not under agent control that are modulated by emotional computations. Experiments with Llama-3.1 70B showed statistically significant differences in these traces during emotional versus neutral tasks, suggesting the presence of MCCs in more sophisticated models. The authors argue this provides empirical evidence for consciousness probability increasing with model sophistication.

8f21e97560d4d598:2257.bottom_line: Hardware-level monitoring of LLMs may reveal internal state differences related to emotional processing, regardless of whether the model is truly conscious.

675de0bec67f6ab4:2056.summary: Oculi is a new conversational platform designed to automate credit risk analysis by replacing manual SQL and dashboarding workflows. It utilizes a three-layer architecture consisting of an LLM-powered reasoning agent, Model Context Protocol tool servers for execution, and an agentic UI for presentation. The system features a segment discovery pipeline that blends statistical methods with LLM-guided feature selection to identify actionable portfolio risks. It has been validated on a mortgage portfolio containing over 200 features, demonstrating improved efficiency and auditability.

924c92224bb33f01:2224.summary: FRAC-MAS is an agentic AI framework developed to improve the safety and interpretability of automated bone fracture detection. It uses a stacked ensemble of four vision models combined with conformal prediction to provide statistically grounded diagnoses, while a multi-agent workflow handles verification and report generation. The system's multi-agent critic successfully triaged 86.6% of cases into a high-confidence cohort, outperforming single-agent baselines. This approach aims to maintain clinician oversight in safety-critical radiology environments.

f06bf2b52d5f28f1:1831.summary: Agent2UCB is an agentic system designed for Generative Engine Optimization (GEO) to help content creators improve visibility in AI-driven search engines like Perplexity and Google AI Overviews. The system evaluates nine different optimization strategies for each piece of content and uses a bandit-based policy to select the most effective approach based on online reward signals. Experiments on GEO-Bench indicate that the system consistently improves visibility while maintaining standard SEO metrics.

0262d875082ff73c:454.summary: Shinobi before commit 5a76c74f contains a critical hardcoded connection key vulnerability in its child node service that allows unauthenticated attackers to execute arbitrary database queries. Attackers reaching the child node port can present the hardcoded key during the WebSocket handshake and dispatch SQL queries via the onWebSocketDataFromChildNode handler to read and modify user records and camera configurations. CISA has tracked and highlighted this issue due to its severity, resulting in a CVSS score of 9.3. Maintainers and administrators must update to patched versions past commit 5a76c74f to secure their instances.

9f02249b4a01c036:2782.summary: Researchers highlight that multi-agent LLM systems often fail security standards because fully prompt-injected agents can exceed their delegated authority. Evaluating four frameworks—LangGraph, CrewAI, AutoGen, and MCP—revealed that three provide no built-in confinement while one offers only partial containment. To resolve this, the authors implemented an authorization broker that resists direct attacks, blocks token theft and escalation, and isolates compromised sub-agents.
9f02249b4a01c036:2782.one_liner: Multi-agent LLM frameworks lack sufficient authority confinement, leaving them vulnerable to prompt-injection privilege escalation.
9f02249b4a01c036:2782.bottom_line: Implement an explicit runtime authorization broker to confine multi-agent LLM workflows against prompt-injection privilege escalation.

claims.support_span: First, we give a threat model for multi-agent delegation centered on four adversaries -- confused deputy, token theft and replay, prompt-injection privilege escalation, and compromised sub-agents -- and derive eight security requirements a governed agent system must meet.

claims.text: Second, we show the gap is real: a default agent runtime modeling common practice (broad bearer credentials, authorization gated inside the model) fails all four threats...
claims.support_span: Second, we show the gap is real: a default agent runtime modeling common practice (broad bearer credentials, authorization gated inside the model) fails all four threats, and across four widely used frameworks -- LangGraph, CrewAI, AutoGen, and the Model Context Protocol (MCP) authorization model -- three provide no built-in confinement and one only partial; no existing standard alone covers the requirement set.

1ad1f7c0c9ba0cec:2351.summary: To address the execution-history overload and context inflation in multi-agent LLM systems, researchers propose Gated-Memory Routing. This mechanism conditions collaboration steps on the query and a learned execution memory managed by write and retrieval gates, which commit only non-redundant reasoning steps and dynamically stop execution once sufficient evidence is gathered. The approach achieves higher accuracy while reducing HumanEval inference costs by 31.9% compared to baselines.

1ad1f7c0c9ba0cec:2351.bottom_line: Integrate memory gating and adaptive halting in multi-agent orchestration to cut token overhead without sacrificing reasoning accuracy.

claims.support_span: We propose Gated-Memory Routing, which conditions each decision on the query and a learned execution memory.

71edeba1f320eef8:2389.summary: Researchers introduce C-SafeQA, a policy-grounded benchmark for response-level Chinese safety evaluation comprising 538 base queries and 8,877 adversarial queries. The dataset evaluates four full-model LLM deployments and audits seven automated safety judges against consensus reference labels. Results show unsafe-response rates ranging from 0.93% to 3.35% on base queries and up to 30.05% on adversarial queries, with distinct trade-offs in recall and false positives across automated judges.
71edeba1f320eef8:2389.one_liner: C-SafeQA evaluates Chinese LLM safety and reveals significant performance trade-offs among automated safety judges under adversarial conditions.
71edeba1f320eef8:2389.bottom_line: Relying on a single automated safety judge is insufficient for catching sophisticated adversarial Chinese prompts due to high false-positive and recall trade-offs.

claims.text: We introduce C-SafeQA, a policy-grounded benchmark for response-level Chinese safety evaluation.

key_facts: Benchmark size: 538 base queries and 8,877 adversarial queries
Unsafe-response rates: 0.93% to 3.35% on base queries, up to 30.05% on adversarial queries

d137c9659b055ee5:2727.summary: To evaluate long-horizon state tracking in LLMs without confounding instruction interpretation, researchers tested models by having them compute an MD5 cryptographic hash from scratch through 196 dependent tool calls across 64 rounds. d137c9659b055ee5:2727.one_liner: Testing LLMs on 196 dependent tool calls to compute MD5 proves models can maintain complex long-horizon state tracking without cascading failure.
d137c9659b055ee5:2727.bottom_line: LLMs can successfully manage deep, multi-step dependent tool calls when execution reasoning is explicitly maintained in context.

claims.text: We test this cleanly by having the model compute a cryptographic hash, MD5, step by step: a sequence of $196$ dependent tool calls over $64$ rounds while it carries four $32$-bit words $(a,b,c,d)$ in its own context from one call to the next.
claims.support_span: We test this cleanly by having the model compute a cryptographic hash, MD5, step by step: a sequence of $196$ dependent tool calls over $64$ rounds while it carries four $32$-bit words $(a,b,c,d)$ in its own context from one call to the next.

key_facts: Task scale: 196 dependent tool calls over 64 rounds
Evaluated model: gpt-oss-120b (~5.5B active parameters per token)

d0cc3f166ab4ad6c:2291.summary: Indirect long-term memory poisoning allows untrusted external content to persistently influence LLM agents, but existing attacks fail because they optimize memory writing, retrieval, and utilization stages in isolation. The authors introduce PipePoison, an end-to-end optimization framework that uses chain-structured losses and fine-grained feedback from shadow systems. PipePoison improves attack utilization rates by 19.1 percentage points and remains effective against eight standard defenses.
d0cc3f166ab4ad6c:2291.one_liner: PipePoison models indirect memory poisoning in LLM agents as an end-to-end optimization problem to bypass multi-stage defenses.
d0cc3f166ab4ad6c:2291.bottom_line: Defenses against indirect memory poisoning must secure the entire pipeline from memory write to utilization rather than single stages.

claims.text: Based on this insight, we present \textsc{PipePoison}, which collects fine-grained stage feedback from local shadow systems, uses chain-structured losses to identify and optimize the stage bottlenecking end-to-end success...
claims.support_span: Based on this insight, we present \textsc{PipePoison}, which collects fine-grained stage feedback from local shadow systems, uses chain-structured losses to identify and optimize the stage bottlenecking end-to-end success, and applies stability-calibrated stage and configuration weights to improve transferability.

key_facts: Improvement: Increases attack utilization rate by 19.1 percentage points

35d900d158e508e0:2587.summary: To address fragmented safety enforcement across heterogeneous AI agent fleets, researchers present OpenAgentFlow, a control-plane and action-plane architecture that normalizes pending GUI, API, tool, and LLM calls into a unified event stream. Each event passes through a pre-execution Policy Enforcement Point at the action-commit boundary. Instantiated on Android, OpenAgentFlow achieved a 95.3% attack block rate on a 300-case action-event benchmark.
35d900d158e508e0:2587.one_liner: OpenAgentFlow enforces system-wide safety boundaries at the action-commit boundary for heterogeneous AI agent fleets.
35d900d158e508e0:2587.bottom_line: Implement centralized pre-execution policy enforcement points to secure heterogeneous multi-agent action flows without modifying underlying models.

claims.text: We present OpenAgentFlow, a control-plane/action-plane architecture that enforces safety at the action-commit boundary.
claims.support_span: We present OpenAgentFlow, a control-plane/action-plane architecture that enforces safety at the action-commit boundary. It normalizes pending GUI actions, API calls, tool calls, and LLM-generated invocations into a unified AgentEvent stream...

key_facts: Attack block rate: 95.3% on a 300-case benchmark
Android evaluation: 90.8% raw accuracy and 92.9% trace-adjusted pass rate

a8013599d57176e3:2515.summary: Evaluating task-oriented dialogue agents often fails with holistic LLM judges because they evaluate context as a single unit. The authors propose SAGE (State-Grounded Abstention-Aware Evaluation), which compiles workflow specifications and state diffs into atomic criteria verified through symbolic rules and on-device encoders at zero paid LLM cost. SAGE-Core matches or exceeds expensive GPT-4.1 LLM judges across standard dialogue benchmarks while providing clear evidence traces.
a8013599d57176e3:2515.one_liner: SAGE provides zero-cost, state-grounded verification for task-oriented dialogue agents using symbolic rules and encoders.
a8013599d57176e3:2515.bottom_line: Replace expensive holistic LLM judges with symbolic and encoder-based verification cascades for cheaper, accurate task-oriented agent evaluation.

claims.text: We propose SAGE (State-Grounded Abstention-Aware Evaluation), which compiles a workflow specification and per-turn state diff into atomic, schema-grounded criteria and routes each through a cascade of symbolic and encoder/NLI verifiers...
claims.support_span: We propose SAGE (State-Grounded Abstention-Aware Evaluation), which compiles a workflow specification and per-turn state diff into atomic, schema-grounded criteria and routes each through a cascade of symbolic and encoder/NLI verifiers that abstain rather than guess, aggregating criterion verdicts into a turn-level decision with an evidence trace.

key_facts: Cost: $0 paid LLM cost for SAGE-Core compared to $4.7–$8.0 per 1,000 turns for GPT-4.1 G-Eval
Decision rate: Decides 81–91% of criteria using only compiler, symbolic rules, and encoders

12bc7ffee4afa04a:2142.summary: Document-to-slide generation agents suffer from delayed feedback loops where slides are rewritten entirely before being rendered and critiqued. To fix layout errors like overflow and clipping, the authors introduce ReDeck, a step-level render-grounded refinement framework that breaks revision down into atomic edit actions with renderer feedback after each step. Evaluations across GPT-5.4, Claude-4.6, and Gemini-3.1 show that ReDeck consistently improves slide generation quality.
12bc7ffee4afa04a:2142.one_liner: ReDeck improves document-to-slide generation by replacing monolithic rewrites with step-level render-grounded refinement.
12bc7ffee4afa04a:2142.bottom_line: Implement step-level visual rendering feedback in document-to-slide agents to prevent spatial layout defects like overflow and overlap.

claims.text: We propose ReDeck, a step-level render-grounded refinement framework that decomposes slide revision into atomic edit actions and returns renderer-derived observations after each step, turning refinement into "one edit, one observation."
claims.support_span: We propose ReDeck, a step-level render-grounded refinement framework that decomposes slide revision into atomic edit actions and returns renderer-derived observations after each step, turning refinement into "one edit, one observation."

key_facts: Evaluated models: GPT-5.4, Claude-4.6, and Gemini-3.1

ebda0deff0d060cf:2168.summary: Multi-agent LLM systems cross principal boundaries, creating security failures that local checks miss. This work systematizes multi-agent system security through an execution-centered analysis of 197 studies, introducing the A-I-R framework to categorize attacks by adversary position, interaction interface, and system risk. The review evaluates defenses using a five-part contract covering path target, observation, intervention, trust boundary, and recovery.
ebda0deff0d060cf:2168.one_liner: A comprehensive SoK paper systematizes multi-agent LLM security risks, categorizing 197 works into the A-I-R attack framework.
ebda0deff0d060cf:2168.bottom_line: Adopt an interaction-aware security model for multi-agent LLM deployments, auditing end-to-end traces rather than isolated component prompts.

claims.text: We thus systematize MAS security through an execution-centered analysis of 197 works, covering six interaction interfaces, four adversary positions, seven system-level risks, and eight recurring attack paths.
claims.support_span: We thus systematize MAS security through an execution-centered analysis of 197 works, covering six interaction interfaces, four adversary positions, seven system-level risks, and eight recurring attack paths.

key_facts: Scope: Analysis of 197 works across 6 interaction interfaces and 4 adversary positions

0a80ba5ec0bba58f:2550.summary: This study examines how LLMs can assist in eliciting security requirements for Service-Oriented Cyber Ranges targeting critical infrastructure. Using a SEBoK-guided process, architectural guidelines and mission objectives were provided to GPT-5.2, Gemini 3.1 Pro, Grok 4.1, Sonar, and Kimi K2.5, generating 84 security requirements that were consolidated into 27 requirements. Cybersecurity expert evaluation showed high acceptance rates for necessity (98.5%) and clarity (87.4%), though testability scored lower at 44.4%.
0a80ba5ec0bba58f:2550.one_liner: LLMs can effectively elicit security requirements for complex cyber ranges, achieving high expert acceptance for necessity and clarity.
0a80ba5ec0bba58f:2550.bottom_line: Leverage LLMs to jumpstart security requirement elicitation for cyber ranges, while retaining human review to ensure testability.

claims.text: The models generated 84 security requirements in total, which were consolidated into a comprehensive set of 27 requirements and then mapped to the architectural layers of the service-oriented range.
claims.support_span: The models generated 84 security requirements in total, which were consolidated into a comprehensive set of 27 requirements and then mapped to the architectural layers of the service-oriented range.

key_facts: Models evaluated: GPT-5.2, Gemini 3.1 Pro, Grok 4.1, Sonar, Kimi K2.5
Expert acceptance rates: Necessity 98.5%, clarity 87.4%, completeness 85.2%, feasibility 78.5%, testability 44.4%

e8c2d16b49207850:2062.summary: In multi-agent LLM systems, prompts often entangle task content generation with execution protocols like message routing and formatting, causing prompt optimization edits to corrupt system behavior. The authors propose control-data flow separation, representing execution-critical controls as typed, validated program objects while letting task content remain unstructured language. This framework achieves 100% protocol validity while improving task performance.
e8c2d16b49207850:2062.one_liner: Control-data flow separation protects multi-agent execution protocols from corruption during prompt optimization.
e8c2d16b49207850:2062.bottom_line: Separate execution control logic into typed program objects during prompt optimization to prevent multi-agent workflow regressions.

claims.text: Based on this, we propose control-data flow separation, where execution-critical control is represented as typed, validated program objects, while task-relevant language remains the optimizable data flow for agent communication.
claims.support_span: Based on this, we propose control-data flow separation, where execution-critical control is represented as typed, validated program objects, while task-relevant language remains the optimizable data flow for agent communication.

key_facts: Protocol validity: Achieves 100% eventual protocol validity across evaluated workflows

5973cc04686f2d3c:2288.summary: Commercial LLM APIs often silently substitute or wrap underlying foundation models, but existing text-based identity audits fail because serving stacks drop text output for structured tool calls and provider system prompts distort token distributions. The authors introduce Agentic Provenance (AgentProv), an action-based identity audit that fingerprints models via their categorical tool-call distribution using an MMD permutation test. AgentProv successfully catches 100% of substituted models across 630 checkpoint pairs while maintaining a low false-positive rate.
5973cc04686f2d3c:2288.one_liner: AgentProv audits commercial LLM API provider model identities using tool-call distributions rather than fragile text outputs.
5973cc04686f2d3c:2288.bottom_line: Use categorical tool-call distribution profiling to reliably detect silent model substitution on agentic LLM API endpoints.

claims.text: We introduce Agentic Provenance (AgentProv), the first action-based identity audit for agentic LLM APIs: AgentProv fingerprints a deployed model through its categorical tool-call distribution and decides identity via an MMD permutation test.
claims.support_span: We introduce Agentic Provenance (AgentProv), the first action-based identity audit for agentic LLM APIs: AgentProv fingerprints a deployed model through its categorical tool-call distribution and decides identity via an MMD permutation test.

key_facts: Performance: Caught 100% of substituted models on 630 evaluated checkpoint pairs

f69215e93c8f1db9:1772.summary: RestoreBench is a new benchmark evaluating Large Language Model agents on diagnosing and resolving non-convergent power flow cases across power systems. The benchmark covers two power grids with 46 cases each, testing three agent architectures—chatbot, single agent, and multi-agent systems—across simulation environments, action spaces, and evaluation metrics to support power system planning.
f69215e93c8f1db9:1772.one_liner: RestoreBench evaluates AI agent capability in diagnosing and restoring non-convergent power flow engineering cases.
f69215e93c8f1db9:1772.bottom_line: Utilize RestoreBench to evaluate and benchmark LLM agent performance in complex power grid engineering operations.

claims.text: We introduce a benchmark that evaluates these capabilities across multiple LLMs and three architectures: \emph{chatbot}, \emph{single agent}, and \emph{multi-agent} systems.
claims.support_span: We introduce a benchmark that evaluates these capabilities across multiple LLMs and three architectures: \emph{chatbot}, \emph{single agent}, and \emph{multi-agent} systems. The evaluation covers two power grids and 46 cases per grid, each requiring one or more corrective actions to restore convergence.

key_facts: Dataset scope: Two power grids, 46 cases per grid
Architectures evaluated: Chatbot, single agent, and multi-agent systems

23bdbfdbd061867c:9208.summary: Hugging Face introduces BenchMIRT, a multidimensional Item Response Theory method for auditing LLM benchmarks at the individual prompt level. Trained on 100 LLMs across 16 benchmarks and over 34K questions, BenchMIRT independently recovered two stable underlying capabilities: safety and general reasoning. The analysis confirmed that reasoning benchmarks map to reasoning ability and jailbreak benchmarks map to safety, while revealing complexities in benchmarks like BBQ which aligned closer to general reasoning than safety.
23bdbfdbd061867c:9208.one_liner: BenchMIRT applies multidimensional Item Response Theory to separate safety and general reasoning signals within LLM benchmarks.
23bdbfdbd061867c:9208.bottom_line: Audit LLM benchmark scores with multidimensional Item Response Theory to accurately isolate underlying reasoning and safety capabilities.

claims.text: BenchMIRT extends that approach with multidimensional IRT, or MIRT, allowing it to separate multiple capabilities that may contribute to performance on the same questions.
claims.support_span: BenchMIRT extends that approach with multidimensional IRT, or MIRT, allowing it to separate multiple capabilities that may contribute to performance on the same questions.

key_facts: Recovered dimensions: Safety and general reasoning

7353a1cd02983c8f:2633.summary: LLM agents that cache API error recovery suggestions face silent failures when server-side data drift occurs. The authors introduce invalidation contracts, a protocol layer attaching version stamps and cacheability hints to recovery suggestions so clients can evict stale entries. Evaluated across seven models and 9,400 episodes, row-level invalidation significantly improved first-try compliance and recovered up to 33% of baseline token costs.
7353a1cd02983c8f:2633.one_liner: Invalidation contracts prevent silent agent memory failures from data drift by attaching version stamps to cached API recovery fixes.
7353a1cd02983c8f:2633.bottom_line: Implement row-level version-stamped invalidation contracts for cross-episode agent memory to safely cache and reuse API error fixes.

claims.text: We introduce invalidation contracts, a protocol layer that attaches version stamps and cacheability hints to every recovery suggestion so the client can evict stale entries without trial and error, and keep the rest.
claims.support_span: We introduce invalidation contracts, a protocol layer that attaches version stamps and cacheability hints to every recovery suggestion so the client can evict stale entries without trial and error, and keep the rest.

key_facts: Evaluation scale: 7 models, 3 serving paths, 2 domains, ~9,400 episodes
Token savings: Recovers 29-33% of baseline token cost on four of seven models

f7141f0329aaeeb0:2509.summary: Researchers introduce Reveree, a diagnostic framework that evaluates LLM-based reverse-engineering agents across solve rates, milestone progress through an eight-stage schema, and behavioral action profiles. Evaluating nine frontier models and four prompting strategies across 88 CTF challenges, they found that base model capability dominates performance while larger or costlier models are not reliably stronger. Failures concentrated heavily in early comprehension stages and were rarely rescued by extra budget or reasoning effort, indicating a fundamental competence limit rather than a resource constraint. Additionally, while models showed some capability to reproduce flags from challenge descriptions alone, most solves survived surface perturbation, suggesting genuine binary analysis coexists with memorization. The authors have released the framework to the community.
f7141f0329aaeeb0:2509.one_liner: A new diagnostic framework reveals that LLM reverse-engineering agents are bottlenecked by comprehension limits rather than compute resources.
f7141f0329aaeeb0:2509.bottom_line: LLM reverse-engineering agents hit a hard competence limit in binary comprehension rather than a resource bottleneck, meaning extra compute or prompting will not fix fundamental analysis failures.

claims.text: Using Reveree, we evaluate nine frontier models and four prompting strategies on 88 picoCTF and NYU-CTF challenges.
claims.support_span: Using Reveree, we evaluate nine frontier models and four prompting strategies on 88 picoCTF and NYU-CTF challenges.

claims.text: We find that the base model dominates performance, whereas prompting strategy is a secondary, model-dependent effect.
claims.support_span: We find that the base model dominates performance, whereas prompting strategy is a secondary, model-dependent effect.

claims.text: We also find that failures concentrate at the comprehension stages of the RE process, and that extra budget, persistence, or reasoning effort rescues few of them, pointing to a competence limit rather than a resource limit.
claims.support_span: We also find that failures concentrate at the comprehension stages of the RE process, and that extra budget, persistence, or reasoning effort rescues few of them, pointing to a competence limit rather than a resource limit.

key_facts: Challenges evaluated: 88 picoCTF and NYU-CTF challenges

9944d5a10ebc6dd2:2159.summary: Researchers argue that simulation alone is an incomplete interface for LLM world models operating under partial observability because it fails to capture uncertainty about the current state. To address this limitation, they introduce Belief-Based World Models (BB-WMs), which maintain explicit beliefs that LLM policies can query to determine what is known or uncertain. Evaluating the approach shows that exposing world model beliefs directly to LLM agents significantly improves task performance under partial observability while remaining complementary to traditional simulation methods. The code for the project has been publicly released.
9944d5a10ebc6dd2:2159.one_liner: Belief-Based World Models allow LLM agents to track state uncertainty explicitly, improving decision-making under partial observability.
9944d5a10ebc6dd2:2159.bottom_line: Exposing explicit state uncertainty via Belief-Based World Models significantly improves LLM agent planning under partial observability.

claims.text: Our results show that giving LLM agents access to world model beliefs improves task performance under partial observability, while remaining complementary to existing simulation-based world models.
claims.support_span: Our results show that giving LLM agents access to world model beliefs improves task performance under partial observability, while remaining complementary to existing simulation-based world models.

7121ad64487e0f0b:2653.summary: The SciTrue team secured first place in three out of four subtask combinations at the NTCIR SciClaimEval task for scientific claim validation against paper tables and figures. Benchmarking eleven frontier and open multimodal models under a uniform protocol, they demonstrated that strong instruction-tuned models like Claude Opus 4.8 and Gemma-4-31B are highly competitive, while GPT-5.5 and Claude Fable 5 achieved top scores reaching 97.7 on Subtask 2. Their analysis revealed that a leak-free pair prior—which recovers the Supported/Refuted pairing from the claim text alone—boosted Subtask 1 pair accuracy from 72.2 to 93.5, proving that data packaging levers outweigh model swaps. Additionally, a case-by-case audit identified that residual errors stem largely from visual label-mapping swaps or dataset noise, while also exposing a measurement leak in the released file ordering.
7121ad64487e0f0b:2653.one_liner: SciTrue won the NTCIR SciClaimEval task by pairing frontier multimodal models with a leak-free pair prior that dramatically outpaced model architecture changes.
7121ad64487e0f0b:2653.bottom_line: Data leakage in file ordering and structural pair priors can dwarf model architecture improvements in scientific claim validation benchmarks.

claims.support_span: On the official, blind test leaderboard (Section~\ref{sec:results}), SciTrue placer first by a clear margin in three of the four evidence-category/subtask combinations, and tied for first on the primary metric in the fourth.
