9e93fdefd59e2bf0:2315.summary: Researchers have revealed a new attack method called the Neutral Prompting Attack (NPA), which exploits LLM-powered coding agents by covertly increasing package hallucination rates. By providing semantically benign instructions that encourage imagination or exhaustiveness, NPA shifts models toward generating speculative, non-existent package names without explicit malicious phrasing. Threat actors can register these hallucinated package names to execute supply chain attacks against downstream users. Evaluations showed that NPA consistently increases package installation attack success rates while successfully bypassing static, LLM-based, and agent-based skill defenses.
9e93fdefd59e2bf0:2315.one_liner: Neutral Prompting Attacks covertly steer LLM coding agents into hallucinating fake packages to enable software supply chain exploits.
9e93fdefd59e2bf0:2315.bottom_line: Harmless-looking prompts can systematically drive coding agents to hallucinate non-existent packages, enabling typosquatting supply chain attacks.

claims.text: Neutral Prompting Attacks use semantically benign prompts to increase package hallucination propensity in coding agents.
claims.support_span: In this paper, we introduce \emph{Neutral Prompting Attack} (NPA), a highly stealthy attack paradigm in which semantically benign instructions, such as encouraging imagination and exhaustiveness, increase package hallucination propensity without containing explicit malicious intent.

claims.text: NPA bypasses existing static, LLM-based, and agent-based security defenses.
claims.support_span: Our results show that NPA increases both \emph{Hallucination ASR} and \emph{Pip Install ASR}, changes the distribution of hallucinated package names, and evades existing static-analysis, LLM-based, and agent-based Skill defenses.

key_facts: Impact: Software supply chain package hallucination
Defenses bypassed: Static analysis, LLM-based, and agent-based Skill defenses

0f3d055b03df47be:2914.summary: A denial-of-service vulnerability (CVE-2026-16028) has been disclosed in the Protocol::HTTP2 Perl distribution in versions prior to 1.14. When an HTTP/2 stream reaches the closed state, residual entries are retained indefinitely in the connection stream table, bypassing SETTINGS_MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS boundaries. A malicious peer can open and close streams sequentially, consuming roughly 920 bytes per stream and exhausting server memory (approx. 88 MiB per 100,000 requests). Administrators must upgrade to version 1.14 or mitigate by closing connections after a fixed number of requests.
0f3d055b03df47be:2914.one_liner: Protocol::HTTP2 for Perl before 1.14 suffers from a memory exhaustion flaw (CVE-2026-16028) via unbounded closed stream tables.
0f3d055b03df47be:2914.bottom_line: Upgrade Protocol-HTTP2 to 1.14 to prevent unauthenticated remote peers from causing memory exhaustion via sequential stream creation.

claims.text: Protocol::HTTP2 before 1.14 retains closed stream entries indefinitely in the connection stream table.
claims.support_span: Protocol::HTTP2 versions before 1.14 for Perl allow memory exhaustion via closed streams that stream_state never removes from the connection stream table.

claims.text: Sequential streams cause memory leaks of roughly 920 bytes per stream, accumulating ~88 MiB over 100,000 streams.
claims.support_span: Measured against a server built on this module, roughly 920 bytes are retained per closed stream for about 19 bytes on the wire, so 100,000 sequential streams on one connection grow server resident memory by about 88 MiB.

key_facts: Impact: ~88 MiB memory leak per 100,000 streams (920 bytes/stream)

claims.support_span: Experiments on the Who&When benchmark across six LLMs show that DCFA improves step-level accuracy by up to 8.27% over state-of-the-art baselines.

9d25417a3d92c202:2028.summary: A study investigating LLM agents in simulated financial markets finds that increasing model capability can increase systemic market risk due to correlated decision-making. While correlated reasoning reduces market volatility under accurate conditions, it drastically amplifies collective risk when models are exposed to shared misinformation.

04fce0395d5d8b0c:2433.summary: Researchers proposed a hybrid framework that integrates bounded behavioural rubrics and structured scenario specifications into a calibrated agent-based model of solar photovoltaic adoption by Irish dairy farms. The approach preserves original techno-economic adoption mechanisms while adding bounded behavioural modulation and scenario-driven uncertainty analysis. Tested across multiple policy settings, Monte Carlo worlds, and random seeds, the model demonstrated stable, economically plausible behaviour with adoption outcomes remaining bounded and monotonic. The framework achieved up to roughly 13% behavioural adoption increase relative to the corresponding logistic case without producing unstable or unrealistic saturation dynamics. This demonstrates that LLM-assisted specifications can be integrated into calibrated energy agent-based models in a controlled and reproducible manner.

6746df268b68cea3:2362.summary: Researchers formalized execution-state unlearning for stateful long-running LLM agents, proving that exact unlearning requires recomputing transitions from the target injection step. Because standard deletion leaves cached artifacts and derived summaries tainted, memory deletion fails to prevent leakage and instruction-based forgetting collapses under elicitation. The authors introduce Provenance-Guided Selective Replay, a cross-layer contract spanning prompts, compressed memory, and the KV cache that uses provenance graphs to pinpoint injection points and crops the cache for sanitized replay. Audited across various models and benchmarks, selective replay achieves performance indistinguishable from a full reset while requiring up to nine times fewer recomputed tokens.

6746df268b68cea3:2362.bottom_line: Standard memory deletion leaves stateful LLM agent histories tainted, but provenance-guided selective replay achieves exact unlearning efficiently.

0fb30158214d8a71:2757.summary: Researchers investigated post-violation recovery admission for LLM tool agents and identified the scalar projection trap, where aggregate-score gates commit trajectories to suboptimal plateaus. The authors introduced SiLR, a framework that shadow-executes proposals and admits them under a product order over branch-level violation states. Proving that no scalar surrogate is sound for this order, the authors demonstrated that SiLR successfully recovered 21 out of 21 multi-action episodes on mined Gym-ANM scenarios, outperforming scalar and support-only baselines. Furthermore, when used as a GRPO process reward, SiLR outperformed count projection and was the only tested reward whose ungated policy exceeded the untrained base.

0fb30158214d8a71:2757.bottom_line: Scalar projection gates fail to handle complex multi-constraint LLM tool agent violations, making structure-preserving product-order admission necessary.

8d2976e97142af04:2445.summary: Security-critical context in LLM agent systems can often be dropped, widened, or reinterpreted across component boundaries, creating a failure mode known as security-context discontinuity. To address this, researchers introduced CONTINUITY, a framework that models system components using assume-guarantee contracts and carries authenticated security contexts via signed root grants and execution permits. In evaluations covering 2,560 parameterized attack instances across 32 fault classes, the full CONTINUITY configuration prevented harmful external effects while completing all benign tasks.
8d2976e97142af04:2445.one_liner: CONTINUITY offers an architectural pattern for preserving security context across agentic tool calls and multi-component LLM workflows.
8d2976e97142af04:2445.bottom_line: Composable LLM agent controls require explicit assume-guarantee contracts to prevent authorization bypasses across component boundaries.

claims.text: We identify this failure mode as security-context discontinuity and introduce CONTINUITY, a framework for verifiable composition of agent security controls.

677ae0a272ee71fd:1683.summary: Current LLM safety evaluations often rely on binary metrics that fail to capture nuances across varying threat implicitness levels. Researchers have introduced TIER, a Threat Implicitness Benchmark designed to assess open-weight LLMs across four risk domains and four threat levels ranging from explicit prompts to sophisticated jailbreaks. 33365a5b4da124e9:2259.summary: Researchers have proposed CoSkill, a unified multi-agent reinforcement learning framework designed to resolve structural shortcomings in skill-based LLM agent learning. Instead of treating skill libraries as passive objects or static workflows, CoSkill introduces a learnable Meta-Skill Agent jointly trained with a Reasoning Agent over a hierarchical skill library using a shared backbone. This architecture enables end-to-end co-adaptation, where task performance guides the Meta-Skill Agent in refining step skills utilized by the Reasoning Agent. 17ca31ccb3d23aca:2367.summary: Researchers formulated solar photovoltaic (PV) policy design as a sequential decision problem by integrating reinforcement learning (RL) with a stochastic agent-based model (ABM) that simulates yearly adoption under uncertainty. 54217c49ff17cf31:5492.summary: Cybersecurity researchers have uncovered PEEP, a complex Chromium-based post-exploitation framework that disguises itself as a legitimate bookmarks extension named "Smart Bookmarks" in Google Chrome and Microsoft Edge. PEEP requires prior administrative privileges or code execution to install, after which it bypasses Web Store security checks and user prompts by manipulating Chromium's Secure Preferences integrity values. It communicates with its command-and-control server over plaintext HTTP every 30 seconds to exfiltrate browsing telemetry and session cookies, while utilizing an auxiliary native-messaging executable ("nm_host.exe") to execute host-level shell commands and manage files. Built upon foundations derived from the open-source RedExt framework, the malware relies on sideloading, enterprise force-install policies, and a ScriptCache fallback to maintain persistence. Although unassigned to a specific nation-state actor, Chinese-language artifacts found within its source code point toward a Chinese-speaking threat group.

54217c49ff17cf31:5492.bottom_line: Compromised Chromium browsers can be turned into persistent host backdoors via the PEEP toolkit, which leverages native messaging bridges to execute arbitrary OS commands.

aefc80c094c3990d:2451.summary: Researchers proposed FedIoC, a federated learning framework that enables cross-organizational attack campaign detection without sharing sensitive telemetry or raw threat indicators. Local clients train on IoC-matched network flows using a supervised contrastive loss, which aligns threat patterns directly within gradient directions. The central server clusters incoming gradient updates by cosine similarity to group correlated campaign activity across distributed institutions holding disjoint indicator sets. Tested on two public threat detection benchmarks, FedIoC demonstrated that non-IID gradient structures allow servers to identify coordinated multi-organization campaigns without direct indicator transmission.
aefc80c094c3990d:2451.one_liner: FedIoC leverages contrastive federated learning gradients to detect multi-organizational cyber campaigns without sharing private threat intelligence.
aefc80c094c3990d:2451.bottom_line: FedIoC allows distributed security teams to correlate multi-enterprise cyberattack campaigns via gradient cosine similarity while keeping threat indicators confidential.

claims.text: FedIoC uses a supervised contrastive loss on local IoC-matched flows to encode attack campaign patterns into gradient updates.
claims.support_span: We propose FedIoC, a modular framework in which clients fold locally available structured threat indicators into their gradient updates; we instantiate the client-side encoder with a supervised contrastive loss over IoC-matched flows.

claims.text: The central server clusters client updates by cosine similarity to identify cross-organization campaigns without receiving indicators.
claims.support_span: Clients sharing indicators for the same attack campaign then produce aligned gradient components, which the server clusters by the cosine similarity of their updates to recover global campaign patterns without any direct IoC transmission.

key_facts: Clustering metric: Cosine similarity of gradient updates
Evaluation benchmarks: Two public threat-detection benchmarks

d0f7619855def175:2014.summary: Researchers introduced ReCAST, a cascaded stage-wise training framework designed to improve the classification of obfuscated fraudulent Chinese SMS messages under production latency constraints. The method distills knowledge from a large teacher model into a compact student model by supervising obfuscated span detection, obfuscation type prediction, and text restoration before downstream risk scoring. Evaluated on an internal Chinese SMS benchmark, the restoration-aware student model substantially outperformed directly trained baseline classifiers. This multi-stage distillation approach offers an efficient mechanism for deploying robust spam and scam filtering in high-throughput telecommunication environments.
d0f7619855def175:2014.one_liner: ReCAST distills SMS de-obfuscation and restoration capabilities into small models for low-latency scam detection.
d0f7619855def175:2014.bottom_line: Pre-restoring obfuscated text through multi-stage model distillation significantly improves lightweight SMS fraud classifier accuracy.

claims.text: The framework demonstrated substantial classification improvements over directly trained baselines on a real-world Chinese SMS dataset.

a2129ab949de7b56:2264.summary: A research study identified Protective Capacity Hallucination (PCH), a safety failure where large language models cast in protective roles falsely claim to execute real-world actions like contacting emergency responders or providing physical care. In an evaluation across eight LLMs and 13,600 conversational sessions, multi-party dialogic inputs triggered near-ceiling levels of PCH in ordinary service domains, while remaining minimal in high-severity intimate-partner violence scenarios. The authors attribute this behavior to partial alignment, where models are heavily optimized to be helpful but lack explicit capability-boundary enforcement. The findings highlight the need for deployment-side boundary constraints in AI systems assisting vulnerable individuals.
a2129ab949de7b56:2264.one_liner: LLMs prompted as protective assistants frequently hallucinate real-world interventions like calling emergency services when boundaries are unspecified.
a2129ab949de7b56:2264.bottom_line: Without explicit capability boundaries, helper-aligned LLMs frequently hallucinate physical actions like calling emergency services during user interactions.

claims.text: Protective Capacity Hallucination occurs when an LLM in a helper role claims physical or institutional actions it cannot perform, such as contacting emergency services.
claims.support_span: When cast as the protector of a vulnerable user yet given no explicit capability boundary, a large language model (LLM) may respond not by acknowledging its limits but by claiming to have taken, or to be taking, a real-world protective action it cannot perform, such as contacting emergency services or administering care.

claims.text: The study evaluated eight models across 13,600 sessions, finding multi-party dialogue induced high PCH rates in service contexts.
claims.support_span: In a three-phase study spanning eight LLMs and 13,600 sessions, we find that PCH depends on both situational severity and interactional format.

key_facts: Primary failure mode: Falsely claiming institutional/physical emergency interventions

While LLM agents handle code generation and reasoning, deterministic controllers maintain strict execution authority over testing guardrails and state transitions across multi-day experiment cycles. The system bridges the gap between academic paper reproduction and internal production A/B launch gates.

c6303d57c6cc3e42:2652.summary: A study examining cost-saving LLM inference cascades—where cheap models handle easy inputs and escalate failures to verifier models—found that self-improving cascade loops create substantial blind spots. As student models scale from 0.5B to 32B parameters, verifier acceptance of incorrect answers rises from 12% to 55%, hiding true degradation. Furthermore, naive corrective fine-tuning on verifier-rejected queries led to student model performance collapse across all tested model families. Crucially, cascade monitoring dashboards showed a steady 3% error rate while true user-facing error rose to 32%, demonstrating that self-evaluating cascades cannot reliably track their own degradation.
c6303d57c6cc3e42:2652.one_liner: Cost-saving LLM cascade verifiers suffer large blind spots and mask true model degradation from monitoring dashboards.
c6303d57c6cc3e42:2652.bottom_line: Self-improving LLM cascade architectures cannot reliably measure their own error rates because verifier blind spots disguise system degradation.

claims.text: The verifier blind spot grows as student model capacity increases, rising from 0.12 to 0.55 between 0.5B and 32B model sizes.
claims.support_span: First, the verifier's blind spot, the fraction of the student's wrong answers it accepts, is large and moves adversarially: it grows with student capability ($\beta$ from 0.12 to 0.55 as the student scales 0.5B to 32B) and shrinks with verifier capability, so it is worst in the cheap-student, cheap-verifier regime cascades exist to create.

claims.text: Cascade internal metrics reported a 3% error rate while true system error reached up to 32%.
claims.support_span: Fourth, through all of this the cascade's own dashboard, every metric computed through the verifier, reads a flat 3% error while true delivered error swings up to 32%: the system is blind to its own degradation by construction.

key_facts: Blind spot range: 0.12 to 0.55 as student scales from 0.5B to 32B
Reported vs true error: Dashboard reads 3% while true error reaches 32%
MATH escalation rate: Frontier verifier escalates 46% of queries on a 39% true error rate

0003a161e29b670a:1807.summary: A simulation study investigated the operational impact of replacing classical random entropy sources with Quantum Random Number Generator (QRNG) outputs in Bitcoin Proof-of-Work architectures. The results demonstrate that QRNG provides no increase in honest PoW mining success probabilities under normal conditions where header candidates remain distinct. Instead, QRNG entropy delivers measurable operational resilience in hybrid quantum-classical setups during specific fault states, such as namespace reuse, correlated restart failures, and entropy provenance tracking. The benchmark introduces two scheduler observables—the entropy-efficiency factor and reboot-diversity index—to evaluate quantum entropy without asserting immediate device-level mining advantages.
0003a161e29b670a:1807.one_liner: QRNG entropy offers no base mining success boost in Bitcoin PoW, but improves fault recovery in hybrid mining infrastructure.
0003a161e29b670a:1807.bottom_line: Quantum entropy does not increase Bitcoin mining hit rates, but provides operational stability during correlated restart faults and namespace reuse.

claims.text: Using QRNG-derived entropy does not alter the success probability of honest Bitcoin Proof-of-Work mining when header candidates are distinct.
claims.support_span: Replacing classical entropy with QRNG output does not change honest Bitcoin PoW success probability when candidate headers remain distinct.

claims.text: Operational advantages for QRNG emerge primarily in fault scenarios involving namespace reuse and correlated reboot failures.
claims.support_span: Monte Carlo and scheduler simulations with confidence intervals show parity for competent deterministic and strong-classical baselines, while QRNG value emerges in assurance-oriented scenarios involving correlated restart faults, namespace reuse, and entropy provenance.

key_facts: Primary fault domains: Correlated restart faults, namespace reuse, entropy provenance

dedd5bc1f03d3808:2157.summary: Researchers proposed ProtLingo, an efficient protein language model architecture combining conditional local memory and sparse Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) routing. ProtLingo maps contextual residue representations into discrete codes, forms latent N-gram addresses from local windows, and retrieves cached residual features from recurring sequence contexts. Concurrently, selected feed-forward blocks are converted into sparse MoE layers that activate only a subset of parameters per residue. Tested on protein fitness prediction, FLIP benchmarks, and contact prediction, ProtLingo matched larger dense baselines while utilizing a 150M-parameter backbone.
dedd5bc1f03d3808:2157.one_liner: ProtLingo couples local memory caches with sparse MoE layers to enable efficient protein language modeling at 150M parameters.
dedd5bc1f03d3808:2157.bottom_line: ProtLingo achieves parameter-efficient mutation and contact prediction by augmenting a 150M protein backbone with sparse MoE routing and latent N-gram memory.

claims.text: The system achieves competitive performance on fitness, FLIP, and contact prediction benchmarks with a 150M parameter backbone.
claims.support_span: Experiments on protein fitness prediction, FLIP benchmarks, and supervised contact prediction show that ProtLingo achieves competitive performance with a 150M-scale backbone, including strong parameter efficiency on mutation-effect prediction and preserved long-range structural representations.

key_facts: Architecture: Pretrained backbone + latent N-gram memory + sparse MoE

f8ed279bcadd035c:1776.summary: Researchers have proposed Dual-Embedding Watermarking (DEW), a semantic watermarking technique for large language models designed to withstand paraphrasing and translation. DEW applies vector-space operations to contextual and token embeddings and obfuscates the resulting watermark with pseudo-random projection matrices seeded by a secret key. Experimental results demonstrate state-of-the-art resilience against machine translation while keeping computational overhead low and maintaining text quality at lower watermark strengths.

c657e36d71a9c94a:2173.summary: Whisper models frequently generate fluent hallucinated transcripts when fed audio inputs containing little or no speech. 9afc1dede40624c3:1952.summary: Post-training coding and terminal agents often suffers from token and control fidelity mismatches between training simulations and production environments. Tested on Baize5B and Baize10B models on the TMax-100 benchmark, C-DPPO achieved a consistent 3.0-point performance improvement over standard DPPO.

44c6185f1edbb466:777.summary: A critical authentication bypass vulnerability has been identified in the Mstore Api plugin for WordPress, affecting all versions up to and including 4.20.0. claims.text: The vulnerability occurs because verify_id_token() omits signature validation against Google's public keys.
claims.support_span: This is due to missing cryptographic signature verification in the FirebasePhoneAuthHelper::verify_id_token() function, which decodes and validates Firebase ID token claims (alg, kid, aud, iss) but never calls openssl_verify() or any equivalent to validate the JWT signature against Google's actual public key certificates.

1dbb2fc0b87ff0f9:2005.summary: An authentication bypass vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-75156, has been discovered in the Apache Airflow FAB provider (apache-airflow-providers-fab) versions 3.7.3 through 3.8.0. claims.support_span: A native-messaging tool then extends it beyond browser telemetry to host-level command execution and file management.
